headline: CF Industries, JERA and Mitsui break ground on Blue Point One low-carbon ammonia plant
summary: The CF Industries (40%) / JERA (35%) / Mitsui & Co. (25%) JV started civil construction in Ascension Parish, Louisiana on a ~US$3.7bn, 1.4-Mtpa ATR ammonia plant with ~2.3 Mtpa of CO2 to be permanently sequestered by Occidental's 1PointFive; first production targeted 2029 (FID was April 2025).
co2crc_note: Blue ammonia plus dedicated CCS with Japanese offtake investors (JERA, Mitsui) is the Asian-export-demand model underpinning Australia's own blue-ammonia/CCS ambitions.
extractor_note: US$3.7bn is the JV project capex, committed at FID in April 2025; today's news is the construction groundbreaking, not a new financial commitment, so amount left null to avoid double-counting. capacity_mtpa 2.3 = CO2 to be captured/sequestered by 1PointFive.

headline: Sarawak reaffirms Kasawari as its first CCUS project, targeting start-up by 2028
summary: Malaysian regional press positioned the PETRONAS-operated Kasawari CCS project offshore Sarawak (Block SK316, ~200 km off Bintulu) as the state's first CCUS project, designed to reinject ~3.3 Mtpa of CO2 stripped from the high-CO2 (~40%) Kasawari gas into a depleted reservoir, with operations targeted by 2028 (PETRONAS has separately flagged bringing first injection forward to 2027).
co2crc_note: Kasawari is one of the world's largest offshore CCS projects and a direct APAC comparator/competitor for Australian offshore storage and cross-border CO2-hub ambitions.
extractor_note: No new money in the item; restatement of a project (FID reached previously). capacity_mtpa 3.3 = designed CO2 reinjection rate. PETROS/Mitsubishi involvement in the wider Sarawak CCUS build-out is as reported, not confirmed on-page (source domain egress-blocked).
